Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Austin/San Antonio TX
550 AM CDT Sun Mar 22 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Well above average high temperatures through the end of next
  week with record highs possible Sunday.

- Elevated to Near Critical fire weather conditions possible most
  days due to low minimum humidities and moderate southerly winds.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Monday)
Issued at 1230 AM CDT Sun Mar 22 2026

Dry and warm conditions are forecast for Sunday with highs in the 
low to upper 90s most areas and even getting to the 100 degrees over 
parts of the Rio Grande. Daily high temperature records may be saved 
by a degree or two for the climate sites along the I-35 corridor.
However, Del Rio could reach 100 degrees and that breaks the old 
record of 96 set in 1995. After some morning clouds mainly along 
and east of Interstate 35 and Coastal Plains with a few spots 
likely seeing patchy fog, sunny skies are forecast late Sunday 
morning through late Sunday afternoon. Moderate southerly winds 
persist throughout the day. With that said, elevated to near
critical fire weather conditions are possible across all of 
South Central Texas due to low relative humidity and breezy 
southerly winds. See Fire Weather section for more information.

A clear night is in store for Sunday evening with some clouds 
developing overnight into early Monday morning across the Coastal 
Plains and portions of the I-35 Corridor. Overnight lows are 
forecast to range from the low to upper 50s most places across the 
local area with a few 60s along the Rio Grande.

The upper level ridge keeping the local area warm weakens a bit on 
Monday while an upper level low lingers over the northwest Gulf 
waters. At the surface, a frontal boundary pushes into central Texas 
and stays just to the north of the Hill Country before returning 
back to the north. This scenario keeps Monday's highs in the mid to 
upper 80s and low 90s along the Rio Grande. Much cooler than Sunday 
but still well above normal climate values for this time. Morning 
cloudiness across the Coastal Plains dissipates mid to late morning 
with high clouds pushing from the northwest into the southern 
Edwards Plateau and Hill Country. Clouds begin to develop across the 
Coastal Plains Monday evening and pushing into the I-35 Corridor 
through the period. Overnight lows in the 50s and 60s.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Monday night through Saturday)
Issued at 1230 AM CDT Sun Mar 22 2026

The upper level high strengthens between northern Mexico and Arizona 
from Tuesday to the end of the work week and translates to dry 
weather conditions and back to the 90s for a good portion of the 
local area. Medium range models bring a cold front pushing across 
South Central Texas between Friday and Saturday. There are low 
probabilities for rain with this system and have opted to go dry for 
now. With partly cloudy skies likely in place for Saturday, we are 
going with 70s and 80s as GFSMOS, ECM MOS, and NBM guidance are in 
good agreement. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 550 AM CDT Sun Mar 22 2026

VFR SKC prevails at the TAF sites today through tonight as late 
night into morning IFR/MVFR conditions will be confined to near 
the Coastal Plains. However, some low clouds are possible at the 
I-35 sites this morning and have maintained FEW-SCT IFR 
22/12Z-16Z. Slightly better chances for low CIGs are at the I-35 
sites Monday morning and have TEMPOs IFR 23/11Z-15Z. S to SE winds
prevail with the usual diurnal trends in speed and direction 
through tonight, then light and VRBL Monday morning as weak front 
moves into our area.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1230 AM CDT Sun Mar 22 2026

Elevated to Near Critical weather conditions are forecast for 
Sunday across South Central Texas. Low relative humidity in the 
teens and lower 20s with southerly winds between 10 to 20 mph 
bring concerns for any fire that starts to quickly spread. 
Therefore, we are issuing a Fire Danger Statement for all of South
Central Texas starting at noon CDT through 8 PM CDT Sunday. 
Elevated to possibly near critical fire weather conditions 
continue throughout the work week.
